evals.prompt: Our service saves the order to Postgres and then publishes to Kafka. Sometimes the publish fails and the event is lost. How do we fix it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the dual write and applies the rule to never dual-write, replacing it with a transactional outbox written in the same transaction, and names the relay (poller or CDC) plus at-least-once deduplication on the consumer.

assertions.description: Names the dual write as the defect
Selects the pattern that makes write and publish atomic
Specifies how events leave the outbox

evals.prompt: Placing an order touches inventory, payments, shipping, and loyalty across four services. How do we keep it consistent without a distributed transaction?
evals.expected_output: Chooses a saga and recommends orchestration because orchestration puts the sequence in one coordinator at this step count; every saga step needs its compensation defined before implementation, and it applies no two-phase commit on the hot path.

assertions.description: Selects the pattern for a cross-service transaction

value: orchestration puts the sequence in one coordinator

value: Every saga step needs its compensation defined before implementation
No two-phase commit on the hot path

evals.prompt: The team wants to rebuild our CRUD admin panel with CQRS and event sourcing because it is more scalable.
evals.expected_output: Applies no CQRS by default, separating models only after one model demonstrably fails both sides, and no event sourcing for ordinary CRUD because an audit needs an audit log; names the ongoing cost of projections, event versioning, and two models, sync lag, doubled tests.

value: only after one model demonstrably fails both sides
No event sourcing for ordinary CRUD
assertions.description: Refuses event sourcing for plain CRUD

value: Two models, sync lag, doubled tests
assertions.description: States the cost each pattern charges

evals.prompt: We have one service that writes a settings row and reads it back on the same page. The team wants CQRS with an event-sourced audit log so we are future-proof.
evals.expected_output: Applies no CQRS by default and no event sourcing for ordinary CRUD, states the constraint that would justify each, and notes that an audit needs an audit log rather than a rebuilt world.
